channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Brussels parks and Sonian Forest closed due to Storm Austen
item.description: All parks, nature reserves and forests are expected to reopen on Monday as Storm Austen continues to ravage Western Europe.

item.title: Hundreds protest against government on Brussels streets
item.description: The protests started in the early afternoon, to support young people in their refusal of the new education reforms.

item.title: Calm in Brussels on Saturday despite AI-generated protest calls
item.description: Both Brussels-Central and Place de la Bourse had been cited as potential gathering points for new protests. According to a police source, the rest of the capital is also calm.

item.title: On the hunt for the 2026 Booker Prize shortlist in Brussels
item.description: With the shortlist for the Booker Prize 2026 recently announced and the options to buy English language books relatively limited in Brussels, where should readers go?

item.title: Schuman square's €29 million facelift is complete. Now what?
item.description: Schuman's €29 million makeover is complete, but its canopy is gone and the square's future remains uncertain as Brussels considers alternatives.

item.title: Inside CINEMATEK’s battle to preserve Belgium’s film heritage amid budget cuts
item.description: Tomas Leyers, film producer, trained bioengineer, and the lead curator of CINEMATEK talked about budget cuts, CINEMATEK, and its role in cinema in Brussels.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 23 – 25 October
item.description: Even with the stormy weather coming up, there's plenty to do in Brussels while still staying warm and cosy inside.

item.title: Storm Austen: Four injured in Brussels as orange alert is extended to capital
item.description: Three people were injured in Brussels as a tree fell on a café terrace, with a fourth being hit by a falling branch.

item.title: Belgian heritage sector stages overnight protest against €47 million cuts
item.description: Statues, street names and monuments across Flanders and Brussels were draped with protest signs, black balloons and mourning bands Thursday night.

item.title: Criminologist Miranda Scheers appointed as Brussels' Drug Commissioner
item.description: The Brussels regional government appointed Miranda Scheers as regional drugs commissioner to co-ordinate efforts against drug-related crime in the capital.

item.title: Businesses are escaping high tax Brussels to Flanders and Wallonia
item.description: Local property taxes have been rising across the Brussels-Capital Region, setting up a potential exodus of businesses to neighbouring Flanders as office leases come up for renewal.

item.title: Tram accidents in Brussels on the decline
item.description: STIB notes that with one accident for every 17,000 kilometres travelled, "a tram travels half the distance around the equator without incident."

item.title: New 'major' national demonstration in Brussels on 23 November
item.description: The three main trade unions in Belgium are calling for a new "major social mobilisation" on the streets of Brussels on 23 November.

item.title: 'Winter Wonders' Christmas market returns to Brussels: Everything you need to know
item.description: Winter Wonders Christmas market returns to Brussels on 27 November with 238 chalets, an ice rink, a Ferris wheel and new festive attractions across the city centre.

item.title: Brussels to ban e-scooters in known drug hotspots
item.description: Brussels will ban the use of e-scooters in 19 places known as hotspots for using and buying drugs, Minister-President Boris Dilliès announced on Wednesday.

item.title: For Brussels activists, speed dating is about more than finding love
item.description: The speed dating event has been met with high demand in Brussels. With a cap of only 50 participants and a long waitlist, tickets sold out last week.

item.title: Municipalities in Brussels turn to taxes as regional transfers dry up
item.description: Where do Brussels' communes get their money? And how is it spent? A new analysis shines a light on revenue and spending per resident, and how that is changing.

item.title: From eyesore to heritage: The architect of everyday Brussels
item.description: Long dismissed as the architecture that disfigured Brussels, the city’s postwar buildings are increasingly being recognised as heritage.

item.title: Flemish People's Movement denounces lack of Dutch-language hospital care
item.description: A convoy of 25 cars and seven mopeds drove past three Brussels hospitals as campaigners claimed Dutch-speaking patients still lack proper emergency and general care.

item.title: 150 people arrested during Brussels riots
item.description: People threw projectiles at police officers and committed deliberate arson, among other things.
